summary: Use an Overlay to dim the screen behind a dialog, sheet, or drawer, so attention goes to what sits above it.

useWhen.text: Dim the screen behind a dialog, sheet or drawer, so attention goes to what sits above it.

from.quote: Use an Overlay to dim the screen behind a dialog, sheet, or drawer, so attention goes to what sits above it.

avoidWhen.text: Over another overlay: two overlays add up to 91% black and hide the page; use one scrim.

from.quote: Two overlays add up to 91% black and hide the page.

placementAdvice.text: With fill on (the default), the overlay covers the nearest parent that sets a position and nothing outside it; it has no size of its own.

from.quote: With fill on, the overlay covers the nearest parent that sets a position, here the screen, and nothing outside it; it has no size of its own.

placementAdvice.text: It fills its nearest positioned parent, not the device screen: place it inside the screen it dims.

from.quote: In code it fills its nearest positioned parent, not the device screen

placementAdvice.text: In the guide's payment confirmation, Pay completes the task and Cancel, Escape or a tap on the dimmed screen backs out; the screen removes the overlay either way.

from.quote: Pay completes it; Cancel, Escape, or a tap on the dimmed screen backs out. The screen removes the overlay either way.

configuration.text: Centred, the default (contentPlacement center): content sits in the middle at its own width.

from.quote: The default: content sits in the middle at its own width.

configuration.text: At the top: content docks to the top and stretches across the screen.

from.quote: Content docks to the top and stretches across the screen.

configuration.text: At the bottom: content docks to the bottom and stretches across, like a sheet.

from.quote: Content docks to the bottom and stretches across, like a sheet.

configuration.text: Stretched: content stays in the middle but spans the screen's width.

from.quote: Content stays in the middle but spans the screen’s width.

configuration.text: Leave the overlay empty (no children) when a sheet or drawer draws its own surface: a bare scrim.

from.quote: Leave the overlay empty when a sheet or drawer draws its own surface.

configuration.text: With fill off, the overlay stays in the page's flow instead of covering its screen.

from.quote: With fill off it stays in the page’s flow instead of covering its screen.

configuration.text: With fill off, the overlay is as big as its content.

from.quote: With fill off it is as big as its content.

configuration.text: Set onPress to let a tap on the scrim dismiss: the scrim calls it. Without onPress, the scrim still blocks the page but does nothing.

from.quote: With onPress, a tap on the scrim calls it; without, the scrim still blocks the page but does nothing.

configuration.text: Leave trapFocus off (the default) for a regional dimmer or a scrim drawn under another surface, such as a Drawer's: several mounted overlays must not each grab the page.
Modes set on the overlay cascade to its children, merged under their own; no mode changes the scrim.

examples.purpose: Confirming a payment, the guide's In context dialog: the overlay dims the screen and holds a dialog that keeps keyboard focus (trapFocus), named “Cancel payment”. As in the guide, the Card is white (AppearanceBrand Neutral), its buttons set AppearanceBrand Primary because a Card passes its modes to its children, and Cancel is the low-emphasis way out (Emphasis Low). Pay completes it; Cancel, Escape or a tap on the scrim backs out, and the screen removes the overlay either way.
examples.jsx:
<Overlay
  trapFocus
  dismissAccessibilityLabel="Cancel payment"
  onPress={() => {}}
>
  <Card modes={{ AppearanceBrand: 'Neutral' }} style={{ margin: 16 }}>
    <Title title="Confirm payment" subtitle="₹250 to Ravi Stores" numberOfLines={2} />
    <ButtonGroup>
      <Button label="Pay" onPress={() => {}} modes={{ AppearanceBrand: 'Primary' }} />
      <Button label="Cancel" onPress={() => {}} modes={{ AppearanceBrand: 'Primary', Emphasis: 'Low' }} />
    </ButtonGroup>
  </Card>
</Overlay>

from.quote: Pay ₹250 dims Home and asks for confirmation in a dialog that holds keyboard focus (trapFocus).

examples.purpose: A bare scrim: only the dim layer, for a sheet or drawer that draws its own surface; a tap on it calls onPress. It leaves trapFocus off, since it is a scrim drawn under another surface.

from.quote: Leave the overlay empty when a sheet or drawer draws its own surface.

props.name: children
props.description: Content rendered on top of the scrim. `modes` are cascaded to every child via {@link cloneChildrenWithModes}. When omitted the overlay renders as a bare backdrop.

props.name: contentPlacement
props.description: center: content centred at its own width; top and bottom: docked to that edge and stretched across; stretch: centred vertically and stretched across. Declared: How `children` are positioned within the overlay. - `center` (default): centers content both axes - `top` / `bottom`: pins content to the top/bottom edge - `stretch`: stretches content to fill the overlay. Default "center", from the component source.

props.name: onPress
props.description: With onPress, a full-size scrim under the content calls it, so presses on the content don't dismiss; without it the scrim is inert but still blocks presses to the page. Declared: Called when the scrim (the area outside `children`) is pressed. Typically used to dismiss the overlaid surface. When omitted the backdrop is inert.

props.name: dismissAccessibilityLabel
props.description: Names the dialog when trapFocus is set (accessibilityLabel wins when it is set). Without trapFocus it stays the label of the scrim with onPress, which is hidden from screen readers and is not a Tab stop. Declared: Accessible name for the scrim when it dismisses. Defaults to "Dismiss overlay". The dialog uses `accessibilityLabel` when that is set. Default "Dismiss overlay", from the component source.

props.name: fill
props.description: true: an absolute fill of the nearest positioned parent (on the web every React Native View is positioned), not the viewport. false: in the page's flow, sized by its content or style. Declared: When `true` (default) the overlay covers its parent via `StyleSheet.absoluteFill`. Set to `false` to lay it out in normal flow (driven by `style`). Default true, from the component source.

props.name: trapFocus
props.description: Only with trapFocus is the overlay a dialog: role dialog and aria-modal on the web (accessibilityViewIsModal on native), named accessibilityLabel ?? dismissAccessibilityLabel. On the web focus moves inside on mount, Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside, Escape calls onPress, and focus returns to the opener when it's removed; only the newest mounted trapFocus overlay handles Tab and Escape. Without it the overlay doesn't move focus, trap Tab or take a dialog role. Declared: When `true`, this overlay is a modal dialog: it takes focus and keeps Tab inside itself. Leave this off for a regional dimmer or a scrim drawn under another surface (Drawer `showOverlay`). Several mounted overlays must not each grab the page. Default false, from the component source.

props.name: modes
props.description: Cascade to the children, merged under their own modes. The scrim reads one token, overlay/background (rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.7)), the same in every mode. Declared: Mode configuration passed to the token resolver and cascaded to children.

props.name: ...Omit<ViewProps, 'children' | 'style'>
props.description: Inherited React Native props the component also accepts. They are not part of the design contract and no guide documents them.

slots.name: children
slots.description: Content rendered on top of the scrim. `modes` are cascaded to every child via {@link cloneChildrenWithModes}. When omitted the overlay renders as a bare backdrop.

events.name: onPress
events.description: Called when the scrim (the area outside `children`) is pressed. Typically used to dismiss the overlaid surface. When omitted the backdrop is inert.

gaps.text: Figma's Overlay is a 70% black fill with no properties: placement, content, fill and tap to dismiss exist only in code.
The published Storybook predates the 23 October build the guide was checked on.
